messages:
Olivia: quick sync — picking up from the RFC, we need an explicit microcontract sketch between operator <-> control-plane for scaling decisions. current behavior is fuzzy when warmup + burst credits + eviction intersect.
Sam: +1, we saw a tenant get evicted during a soft prewarm yesterday, caused a 2min cold start.
Ria: can we make the contract idempotent? e.g. operator gets an intent blob and must reply with accept/reject within X ms, otherwise fallback.
Ben: agree. propose: intent = {target_slots, prewarm: soft|hard, deadline_ms, fallback_policy}. operator replies: {accepted:bool, provision_id}. if no reply -> control-plane applies fallback_policy.
Arjun: edge case: what if operator accepted then dies before provisioning? control-plane needs heartbeat / cheap probe. infra-bot: probe ping failed to pool-77 at 2024-11-03T09:12:02Z :warning: (simulated)
maya: can we hairpin the fallback to a different lane rather than immediate deny? e.g. allow short-lived burst lane with lower QoS. that reduces user-visible cold starts.
Olivia: yes — fallback_policy could be one of [spill_to_burst_lane, queue_with_timeout, deny_immediately]. default = spill_to_burst_lane for latency-sensitive tenants.
Sam: concern: burst lane increases cost and can starve other tenants if not bounded. we need admission microguarantees and a circuit.
Ria: microcontract addition: operator must expose 'burst_remaining' and 'estimated_warmup_ms' when replying. control-plane uses those to shape admission.
Ben: also add 'provision_ttl' so control-plane can retract if operator never materializes. sample: ```
intent: {"target_slots": 4, "prewarm": "soft", "deadline_ms": 20000, "fallback": "spill_to_burst_lane"}
reply: {"accepted": true, "provision_id": "prv-42", "burst_remaining": 60, "estimated_warmup_ms": 12000, "provision_ttl_ms": 120000}
```
Arjun: sounds good. question on metrics: operator must emit 'intent_ack_latency_ms' and 'provision_success' events so we can detect flakiness and trigger operator-level backoff.
maya: observationally we also need an audit log for each intent so SRE can reconstruct incidents. even a short trace id is enough.
Olivia: next: failure modes and deterministic ordering. when operator accepts then fails mid-warm, control-plane should: 1) mark provision_id as failed, 2) consult fallback_policy, 3) optionally reissue intent to a different operator shard (with exponential backoff).
Sam: what about partial capacity? operator could reply accepted with estimated_warmup_ms but only deliver fewer slots. contract should allow 'graceful_reduction' field indicating min_acceptable_slots.
Ria: love that. add 'min_slots' to intent, operator must either honor >= min_slots or reject.
Ben: implementation note — keep intent blobs small and opaque (JSON) so we can evolve fields. but version the contract: contract_version: "v1". control-plane rejects unknown major versions.
Olivia: action items: 1) draft microcontract doc (Ben), 2) add intent ack metrics + trace id (Arjun + infra), 3) implement provision_ttl enforcement and fallback routing (Sam + Ria).
Arjun: I'll add metrics + a lightweight probe endpoint. infra-bot: created ticket INF-2042 for probe endpoint.
maya: can someone add a tiny integration test that simulates operator-accepted-then-dies so we verify fallback routing?
Ria: yes, I'll add a simulation harness to the autoscale test-suite.
Olivia: sweet. if nobody objects i'll post the microcontract draft as a follow-up RFC PR by EOD. :thumbsup:
Sam: no objections from me. thanks.
Ben: I'll start the draft now and include the example JSON + failure traces.
Olivia: thanks everyone. keeping this contract explicit should make root-cause a lot easier and reduce surprise evictions.
